term: entailing selection of a labeled arrangement
definition: Selects a p requires p true at the designated arrangement a and requires every arrangement where p is true to equal a. FullTruth records all endpoint and immediate-link equalities. EvidenceOnly is reused literally from HistorySelection: candidate truth depends only on the entire admitted evidence vector. CompleteRequiresSelection a adequate is the separate OPEN local requirement that every candidate judged adequate for this actual chain passes Selects; AcceptsUnselected is its explicit rival, accepting some candidate true at a and also true at an explicitly distinct arrangement b; failure of actual truth does not count.
note: This is informational entailment, not causal production, epistemic access or independent explanatory adequacy. An exact labeled-link table selects its arrangement, including when it is a mere description of the target; a tautology does not. No asymmetry, transitivity or well-foundedness of adequate is imposed: adequate is a supplied judgment on candidate propositions, not a causal relation. The bridge requires an independent philosophical defense before any real-world application. Intrinsic, noncontrastive and probabilistic accounts may accept explanation with surviving alternatives. The model permits all these unproved judgments; neither selection nor cardinality makes any one true. See docs/notes/ordering-cardinality-1003.md. TruthfulRivalControls rejects every judgment accepting only actual-false candidates, conditionally witnesses a truthful nonselecting candidate when acceptance of constant true is supplied, and proves the truthful rival incompatible with the selection requirement. This is not a proof that a tautology adequately explains reality.
